invented: finally snapped up the last stretch of the river road (The briefing says only that a trading post opened; it says nothing of a last stretch or a takeover.) | the locals say it's just convenient for them (Invented reported speech from unnamed locals.) | [minor] The Red Gully Raiders have been quiet lately (Asserts the raiders' recent behaviour, which the briefing never mentions.) | [minor] likely bringing more snow than usual (Adds scale to the cold snap forecast.) | anyone trying to reach the distant coast (Introduces a coast the briefing does not name.) | [minor] This will probably make travel difficult (Implied consequence of the cold snap, beyond what the briefing gives.)
comment: The bulletin is readable and leads with the right news, but it embroiders both items with unsupported claims: the 'last stretch' of road, the locals' quote and a coast the briefing never names. The voice is only mildly wry, and 'One assumes' reads more like speculation than dry wit.

invented: [minor] This leaves the contested flats open for other traders. (An implied consequence stated as fact. It also contradicts the later claim that the flats remain contested.) | [minor] Their caravan moved through the eastern ford (The briefing says the caravan reached the ford, not that it moved through it. This is also old news presented as current.)
comment: The bulletin leads correctly with the abandoned camp. It then recycles old news as new and lifts jokes and whole sentences verbatim from earlier bulletins ("more guards than goods", "stay inland", "profitable week"). It also contradicts itself about whether the flats are open or contested.

invented: The Ashen Hand's raiders are back on the Merrow road with fresh stores. (Presents a new raid; the briefing says nothing new happened.) | One homestead lost its roof and two others were looted of their grain. (Retells old news as new and contradicts it: three homesteads and grain are not in the briefing.) | prices for goods seem steady (Invents price information; the earlier bulletin implied prices rose.) | The Kinn tribe has shifted their grazing routes south to avoid the old fire line. (Invents a new movement and a fire line. This is not in the briefing, and the fires were in the south.) | They claim they are simply moving livestock (Invents a claim and livestock.) | [minor] caravan patrols (Embellishes caravans into patrols.)
comment: On a quiet week it invents a fresh raid, new figures and Kinn movements, and it contradicts itself by calling the week quiet straight after reporting attacks. The voice is flat and repeats earlier material instead of commenting drily.

invented: Tomas Quell's last known position was in the northern sector (Briefing gives no location for Quell; 'northern sector' is invented.) | [minor] before he vanished into thin air (Briefing only says the Dispatch is seeking news of him; vanishing is an inference stated as fact.) | The Brine Coast League seized three Black Fen Raiders' vessels on the south channel. (Invented event and number; contradicts the briefing, which says Black Fen Raiders burned a ferry.) | ceased operations (Contradicts the briefing: the Dispatch stopped sending reporters toward Lowmere, not all operations. The 'I suspect' framing does not cover a claim that contradicts the facts.)
comment: It replaces the ferry burning with an invented seizure of three vessels, and it adds a location for Quell that the briefing never gives. Each item is a single flat sentence, well short of the length and format asked for, with almost no wry voice.

invented: Perhaps they simply want to avoid further disputes with the Scythe Tooth pirates. ('Further' presupposes existing disputes between the Gorse Clans and Scythe Tooth, which the briefing never mentions.) | [minor] Its members have asked who is paying for the defense. (Repeats an old-bulletin line as if new and adds 'for the defense'.)
comment: The second paragraph copies the latest bulletin almost word for word and presents the old raid news as current, breaking both the old-news rule and the no-reuse rule. The closing paragraph is a muddled single-sentence guess that adds nothing, so only the lead item does any real work.

invented: Saltreed remains empty as usual. (The briefing gives nothing about the colony's state. Calling it empty is an invented and contradictory claim about the inside of the colony.) | The Combine says harvests are good elsewhere. (The briefing places the good harvests along the delta, not elsewhere. This contradicts it.) | [minor] Ditch Kings stole a grain barge on the delta. (The briefing says they robbed a barge; stealing the barge itself goes beyond that.)
comment: The lead item is right, but the bulletin invents an 'empty' Saltreed and moves the harvests 'elsewhere', contradicting the briefing. The third paragraph is padding, and the voice is flat with little of Ilse's wry edge.

invented: [minor] They expect every traveler to pay their share before crossing the narrow pass. (Embellishes the toll demand with details of who pays and when, plus 'narrow pass'.) | [minor] Vex's Crew has two settlements, but they seem content with doing nothing. (Characterises the pirates' activity, which the briefing does not describe.) | Imperial envoys visited two outlander towns yesterday. (Invents a date ('yesterday') and presents old news as new.) | Raiders took it near the gorge in broad daylight (Repeats an old item as if it were current news; 'broad daylight' also comes only from the earlier bulletin, not the briefing.)
comment: It copies the earlier bulletin's wagon joke word for word and re-presents both old items as fresh news, dating the envoy visit to 'yesterday'. Its final sentence is also garbled.

invented: [minor] at the upcoming fair (The briefing says the Accord is hosting the fair now, so calling it upcoming misstates the timing.)
comment: The second paragraph copies the latest bulletin word for word and re-presents old news, which breaks the no-reuse and old-news rules. The lead item is padded with a muddled lantern guess that makes little sense.

invented: The Lancers are no longer feared for their aggression, though they still operate with impunity. (A new claim about the Lancers' standing and activity that the briefing does not give, stated as fact.) | The skirmishes continue without bloodshed (Invents ongoing skirmishes and their outcome; the briefing reports no fighting.) | Neither faction has yet secured any catch in recent waters (States the earlier bulletin's joke as a factual report on the current situation.) | [minor] suggests a quiet shift in pirate morale (Implies a consequence of Malley's death that the briefing does not support.) | [minor] making the conflict purely ideological (Characterises the war in a way the briefing does not support.) | [minor] formally declared war (Embellishes the manner of the declaration.) | [minor] their volatile nature (Unsupported characterisation of the factions.)
comment: Re-reports the old war declaration as news, recycles the earlier fishing joke, and invents bloodless skirmishes and the Lancers' current reputation. Phrases like 'local law enforcement' and 'operate with impunity' read like modern newswire rather than Odile's dry frontier voice.

invented: Now, she was the only one left to carry that memory. (Contradicts the briefing: Lene, Joska's wife and Tamsin's mother, is not said to be dead.) | the small scar on his neck where Malley had tried to stab him (Invents a specific wound and attack the briefing never mentions.) | [minor] Joska's laugh when he told stories about how pirates were nothing but rats (Invented memory and characterisation of Joska's sayings.) | Tamsin knew the ground was unstable there (Invents a fact about the camp's terrain.) | I'm going to find out who is really behind that (Implies a hidden culprit beyond the Lancers that the story never suggests.) | [minor] gripped the rifle tight (A weapon not named in the briefing.)
comment: The scene runs to about 200 words, well over the 120 limit, and names emotions outright ('grief mixed with a fierce determination'). It also invents several facts, including erasing Lene and a conspiracy, and contradicts itself: she grips the rifle, then later pulls it from a 'shoulder holster'.

invented: [minor] Red Gully Raiders are still operating in their usual territories. (The briefing gives only a settlement count. It says nothing about ongoing activity or territories.) | [minor] The current arrangement of factions remains unchanged for this cycle. (This is the first bulletin, so there is no earlier state to compare against. 'Unchanged' is an unsupported inference stated as fact.)
comment: The bulletin reads like a flat report with almost none of Ilse's dry wit. It crams both new items into one paragraph and pads with vague filler about the factions instead of using the settlement counts. It also falls short of the word target.

invented: [minor] The Glimmer Coast Company continues its movement. (The briefing only says a caravan reached the eastern ford, which is old news; ongoing movement is implied.) | [minor] They are noted for their consistent profitability. (This restates an earlier joke as a plain fact; the briefing gives no profitability information.)
comment: The bulletin is flat and repetitive, with almost none of Ilse's dry wit. Two of its three paragraphs rehash old news as if it were current, which pads a one-item week. The lead item is undersold, and calling it a 'quiet week' at the end doesn't rescue the dull, report-like prose.

invented: The Kinn of the Long Grass are moving south. (The briefing does not say this. The earlier bulletin placed the grass fires in the south, not the Kinn's direction, and it is presented as current news.) | Their intentions remain unstated, as usual. (This contradicts the earlier bulletin, where the Kinn said they were not looking for trouble.) | [minor] The Ashen Hand remain in their usual pattern of raiding. (It turns one covered raid into an ongoing 'usual pattern', stated as fact.)
comment: The bulletin restates old news as if it were current and gets the Kinn wrong, contradicting the earlier report. It is also flat and short, with none of Ilse's dry wit and no use of quiet-week material such as faction sizes or the date.

Accurate but lifeless: it restates the briefing with no dry wit or persona, crams all three new items into one paragraph, and falls well short of the 70–130 word target. Calling it 'a quiet week' right after a burned ferry and a missing reporter reads as a contradiction rather than a joke.

invented: Scythe Tooth raids continue in a quadrum. (The briefing reports only past raids at three settlements. It does not say they are continuing, so this presents old news as ongoing.)
comment: The lead item is a bare one-sentence restatement. The second item recycles old news as if the raids are still happening. The closing paragraph is empty filler that pads the bulletin and lacks Odile's sardonic precision.

invented: [minor] The Calder Combine reports continued good harvests along the delta. (Recasts old news as a fresh report and adds 'continued'; no new harvest report is in the briefing.)
comment: The lead item is a bare copy of the briefing line with no wit or development, and the old harvest news is recycled as if it were a new report. Four flat paragraphs and about 55 words miss the requested format and length, and Ilse's dry voice is barely present.

invented: [minor] active this cycle (The briefing gives only the settlement count, not any activity.) | [minor] They are still counting losses against their current tally. (Stated as fact, not as a guess, that the Covenant is still tallying losses. This stretches the old wagon story.)
comment: The bulletin is too short (about 45 words, against 70–130) and mostly flat. The lead item gets one bare sentence with no wit, and the closing line is muddled and asserts ongoing losses the briefing doesn't support.

invented: [minor] The Ninefingers Gang remains silent. (Asserts their quiet continues this week; the briefing has no new information on the gang.)
comment: The lead item is a single sentence copied from the briefing, and the old news is padded out into three more paragraphs. It also reuses the earlier bulletin's 'river is full and the fish are foolish' line, which the task forbids, and the voice is flat with almost no wit.

invented: [minor] Cinder Rest is quiet this week. (The reporter has no knowledge of the colony's internal affairs; quietness is an inference stated as fact.) | [minor] The faction sizes remain as previously noted. (No earlier bulletin noted faction sizes, so this misrepresents the record.)
comment: The lead item is accurate, but the voice is flat and barely sardonic, and the third paragraph is filler that breaks the 'never pad' rule while misstating the colony and the earlier bulletins. The second item adds nothing beyond restating old news.

invented: The silence of the Lancers' camp pressed in. (Places Tamsin at the enemy-held camp. This is unsupported, and the scene itself later puts the camp on a distant horizon.) | the charred remains of their shared gear (Invents a fire and shared possessions the briefing never mentions.) | [minor] the broken weapon (Adds an unmentioned object, presumably Joska's, as a fact.) | [minor] Lene’s face, etched with exhaustion, was visible in the shadows. (Places Lene in the scene and describes her state, neither of which the briefing gives.)
comment: The setting contradicts itself: Tamsin is at the Lancers' camp and also gazing at it on a distant horizon. It also invents charred gear and a broken weapon, and leans on cliché ('knuckles white'). The sharpening ending gestures at intent but never names Malley's successor or what the hunt is for.

invented: [minor] before winter sets in (Adds a season context the briefing lacks; it is Aprimay (spring), so winter is not imminent.) | [minor] three scattered settlements on the edge of the map (Adds 'scattered' and a location the briefing does not give; 'map' is also game-meta language.) | [minor] four remaining settlements ('Remaining' implies losses the briefing never mentions.)
comment: It covers both items in order and frames most guesses properly, but it piles on unsupported colour ('remaining', 'scattered', 'before winter') in a spring bulletin. 'Edge of the map' breaks the frontier voice, and several sentences run well over 20 words.

invented: [minor] leaving behind nothing but smoke and silence (Adds detail of the abandonment (smoke) that the briefing does not give.) | The Tannerfolk claim this means they won (Invents a Tannerfolk claim or statement not in the briefing.) | [minor] a stalemate that keeps prices high (Calls the war a stalemate and links it to prices, neither of which the briefing states.) | reached the eastern ford earlier this week (Invents a timeframe and presents old news as recent.) | [minor] with more guards than goods (Attaches a detail from an earlier bulletin to this caravan as fact. It also reuses an old line.)
comment: The lead item is right, but the bulletin invents a Tannerfolk victory claim and a timeframe. The whole second paragraph rehashes old news and reuses the earlier 'more guards than goods' joke. The 'ran out of fuel' line is also muddled.

invented: Two homesteads on the Merrow road remain lost to their raiders (The briefing says the homesteads were raided and lost stores, not that they are still lost or held.) | traders travel in pairs to pay the toll (No toll is mentioned anywhere; this invents a fact and a cause.) | moving northward (The briefing gives no direction for the Kinn's movement.) | [minor] keep the Kinn of the Long Grass moving (This presents the earlier grass-fire news as an ongoing current situation.)
comment: On a quiet week this rehashes old news as if it were current, and it recycles earlier jokes almost verbatim (doubled prices, trouble finding someone). It also adds unsupported details: a toll, a northward direction, and homesteads still 'lost'.

invented: the Rim Dispatch remains the only settlement left standing (Contradicts the briefing: the Brine Coast League has 6 settlements and the Black Fen Raiders have 3.) | [minor] its missing reporter (The briefing says only that the Dispatch is seeking news of him. Calling him missing states an inference as fact.) | [minor] entirely (Adds emphasis the briefing does not give.)
comment: The closing line contradicts the briefing's faction counts by calling the Dispatch the only settlement standing. The remark that staff are 'more valuable than our local correspondents' is muddled, which leaves an otherwise plain bulletin confusing and inaccurate.

invented: shut their markets to outsiders on day forty-seven (The briefing gives day 47 as today's date, not the date the markets closed.) | This ends the fur-for-grain trade that kept prices low. (This contradicts the earlier bulletin, which described the prices as high, and states an unsupported consequence as fact.) | last month (The briefing gives no timing for the cold snap.) | [minor] in quick succession (This embellishes the manner of the raids; the earlier bulletin said only 'in a quadrum'.) | [minor] Now Scythe Tooth pirates have raided three settlements ('Now' presents old news as if it were new.) | [minor] The Ferrow Mutual is organizing patrols (This overstates what was reported: the Mutual only asked its members to share patrols.)
comment: The lead invents a date and a consequence that contradicts the earlier report of high prices. The second paragraph rehashes old news as if it were current and recycles the 'who is paying' joke, which pads a one-item week.

invented: [minor] even if the Combine claims their harvest is finally good enough to spare (The briefing says only that harvests were good; that there is enough to spare is an embellishment.) | [minor] while imperial shuttles drift over the eastern mountains (The sighting is old news but is written in the present tense, implying it is still happening.)
comment: The bulletin leads correctly with the barge robbery and uses the faction counts accurately. However, it presents the old shuttle sighting as current activity and embellishes the harvest. The voice is serviceable but less sharp than in the earlier bulletin.

invented: [minor] They are short on supplies (The briefing records one lost wagon. A general supply shortage is an added consequence.)
comment: The second item restates last time's wagon theft as a full news item, padding a one-item week with old news. Both paragraphs recycle earlier jokes ('polite smiles and long scrolls', 'short on… long on complaints') instead of writing fresh wit.

invented: merchants are already queuing to see if they can afford a piece (Invented event; the briefing says nothing of queues or sales.) | [minor] The trade fair at Lantern Hill remains open (Infers the fair's current status, which the briefing does not give.) | [minor] leaving three settlements in a strange lull (Embellishes the gang's quiet into a lull across all its settlements.) | [minor] continue to report a good fishing season (Presents old news as ongoing, which the briefing does not state.)
comment: There is only one new item, but the bulletin pads it with two paragraphs of old news and reuses the earlier bulletin's jokes almost word for word. It also invents queuing merchants and runs past the word limit. The 'only nine settlements' line makes little sense, since nine is the largest faction count.

invented: [minor] His Lancers remain the only pirate settlement left in the region. ('Left' implies other pirate settlements were lost, which the briefing does not say.) | [minor] their fleet (The briefing gives the Lancers no fleet; the phrase presupposes one inside a guess.)
comment: The lead item is plain and accurate. The second paragraph presents the already-covered war as new and reuses the earlier bulletin's sentences almost word for word, including the fish joke, which breaks two explicit instructions. The closing line about a 'quiet week' also contradicts the news of a captain's death.

invented: Tamsin sat in the mud where Joska had fallen (Places Tamsin at the camp the Lancers still hold; the briefing never says she was there.) | [minor] the Lancers' ruined camp ('Ruined' is an added embellishment; the briefing only says the Lancers still hold the camp.) | the cold, rusted hilt of his old blade (Invents a specific item, Joska's blade, that the briefing never mentions.) | The memory of his final scream (Implies Tamsin witnessed Joska's death, which the briefing does not support.) | imagining Captain Malley's new face, the one who would hunt Cinder Rest for revenge (Muddles the dead Malley with the unnamed new captain, contradicting the briefing.)
comment: The scene invents a weapon and a witnessed death, wrongly puts Tamsin at the enemy-held camp, and confuses Malley with the new captain. It also names emotions outright ('the anger felt different'), and the ending is muddled: it is unclear who 'he' is in 'never found peace', and 'The hunt began' is a flat close rather than a clear statement of what Tamsin means to do.

Accurate and clear, but flat as a ledger: there is no trace of Ilse's dry, wry voice, and the second paragraph just recites the faction counts. It also runs only about 50 words, under the requested length.

invented: [minor] This follows the ongoing skirmishes with the Tannerfolk. (Implies a sequence or cause for the abandonment that the briefing does not state. It also recasts the war as 'skirmishes'.)
comment: The output is accurate on the lead and easy to follow, but it lacks Ilse's dry wit entirely. The faction counts are recited flatly, and at about 50 words it falls well short of the requested length. Calling the week 'dull' also undercuts the one real piece of news.

Accurate and free of invented facts, but the bulletin is thin and bland: it falls short of the word count, recites the faction sizes without much wit, and misses easy dry material like the date or the old raids. It reads as filler rather than Ilse's sharper voice from earlier bulletins.

invented: [minor] This quiet week (The briefing gives three new items, so calling the week quiet misstates it.)
comment: Accurate but flat. There is no dry wit, it uses stiff connectors like "Furthermore", and it is well under the word count. The items are crammed together and badly paragraphed, the faction counts read as padding, and calling a week with three items "quiet" contradicts the briefing.

invented: [minor] This development follows the recent crop losses in the northern basin. (Implies a causal link between the crop losses and the market closure that the briefing does not give.) | Scythe Tooth raids continue across the rim. (Presents old news as ongoing and widens it 'across the rim'. The briefing only reports raids at three settlements, already covered.) | The Ferrow Mutual continues to organize patrols. (The briefing says nothing about Ferrow patrols. Even the earlier bulletin said only that it asked members to share patrols, not that it is organising them.)
comment: Flat and voiceless, with none of Odile's sardonic understatement. The second paragraph rehashes old news as if it were still happening and asserts unsupported ongoing patrols instead of commenting drily on a quiet week.

invented: [minor] It is a quiet week here in Saltreed. (The reporter is near Saltreed, not in it, and knows nothing of the colony's state.) | [minor] They seem to be active this cycle. (Infers ongoing activity from a single robbery, though 'seem' softens it.)
comment: The bulletin is accurate in substance but flat and far too short, about 45 words against the 70 to 130 asked for. It has almost none of Ilse's dry wit, and the faction-count paragraph just restates the briefing without any wry comment.

invented: [minor] The Iron Covenant remains at eight settlements. ('Remains' implies an unchanged earlier count; the briefing gives only the current number.) | [minor] Vex's Crew still controls two settlements. ('Still' implies continuity that the briefing does not state.)
comment: Accurate on the toll news but flat and repetitive ('demanded… demands… demanding'), with little of Ilse's wry bite. At about 55 words it falls short of the 70–130 target, and calling the week 'remarkably dull' right after the toll demand undercuts the lead.

invented: [minor] Jade sculptures are drawing the eye at Lantern Hill. (Briefing names one jade sculpture, Gladwater's; the plural and the dropped source distort it.) | [minor] The Accord's trade fair is underway. (Briefing only says the Accord is hosting a fair; 'underway' is an inference stated as fact.)
comment: The lead item drops Gladwater, the actual news, and turns one sculpture into several, so the story is lost. The bulletin is also well under length, calls a week with news 'quiet', and its jokes are flat lists of faction counts with little of Ilse's wit.

invented: [minor] The Lancers now control only one settlement. ('Now ... only' implies they lost settlements, possibly because of Malley's death. The briefing just gives 1 settlement.)
comment: Accurate and readable, but almost voiceless: it reads like a list of briefing facts with none of Odile's sardonic wit. Calling it 'a quiet week' right after a pirate captain's death falls flat rather than landing as understatement.

invented: Tamsin stood over the cooling form of her father, the grit of the Lancers' camp clinging to her scavenged gear. (The briefing never places Tamsin at the Lancers' camp or at the fight. This invents her presence at his death.) | She traced the shallow cut near his ribs, a souvenir from Malley. (This is a specific wound the briefing does not give, and 'shallow cut' undercuts Malley having maimed him.) | [minor] The new captain’s oath echoed in the sudden silence. (It implies Tamsin heard the oath in person. The briefing only says the captain swore revenge.) | [minor] She turned toward the fortified entrance. (The camp having a fortified entrance is added detail.)
comment: The scene puts Tamsin at the Lancers' camp and invents a shallow wound that clashes with Joska being maimed. It also ends on an ambiguous turn toward an entrance instead of stating what she means to do.

invented: [minor] It will be a miserable week (Adds a duration and severity to a forecast the briefing gives plainly.) | [minor] They are joined by the Red Gully Raiders with three ('Joined by' can read as an alliance between the factions, which the briefing does not state.)
comment: The first two items are accurate and drily witty, and the guess about the mud is properly hedged. The faction paragraph is flat, and 'joined by' wrongly hints at an alliance.

The bulletin is accurate and leads correctly with the abandoned camp, and 'a better spot to be miserable' is a decent dry line. The rest is flat: the Glimmer Coast paragraph is filler without a joke, and at about 60 words the piece falls short of the requested length.

invented: They continue to operate as they always have, despite the previous raids. (Stated as fact without support. It contradicts the briefing, which says Merrow caravans changed to travelling only in pairs.)
comment: The settlement counts are correct and the quiet week is acknowledged honestly. But the bulletin is flat and almost witless, nothing like the dry Ilse of earlier bulletins, and it closes with an unsupported claim that contradicts the caravans-in-pairs change.

invented: [minor] It is a quiet week for the news, which is a change of pace. (Calls a three-item week quiet and implies a past pace, though this is the first bulletin.)
comment: The bulletin is accurate and readable, but it misses the obvious link between the missing reporter and the Dispatch pulling reporters from Lowmere. The closing 'quiet week, change of pace' line contradicts the busy briefing and makes no sense in a first bulletin.

invented: The Scythe Tooth pirates have struck three settlements. This follows the previous raids I reported. (Presents old news as new and implies a second, separate set of raids that the briefing does not report.) | [minor] The Ferrow Mutual is still debating the cost of their shared patrols. (Claims the debate is ongoing; nothing in the briefing says what happened with the patrols since.) | [minor] A quiet week is, in itself, a notable occurrence. (Calls the week quiet even though there was new news: the Gorse Clans closed their markets.)
comment: The lead item is handled adequately. The second paragraph rehashes old raid news as though it were fresh and implies new raids. The closing calls the week quiet despite real news, and it reads as filler.

The bulletin is accurate and clear. It leads with the barge robbery and frames the Combine's losses as a guess, so nothing is invented. The wit is thin, though: the Empire and faction-count paragraphs read as generic filler rather than Ilse's sharper dry voice.

invented: [minor] The Iron Covenant still lacks that supply wagon lost to the raiders. (The briefing does not say the wagon was never recovered; this inference is stated as fact.) | [minor] The Empire continues its expansion of influence through these new demands. ('Expansion of influence' is an implied consequence, framed as fact.)
comment: The lead item is accurate and has a dry guess in it, but the second paragraph reads as padding. It rehashes old news, states two inferences as fact and ends on a flat, analytical line that drops the persona's wit.

The bulletin is accurate and clear, but the voice is flat. Only the 'one assumes' line shows any wryness, and the last two items just restate old news and the date without the dry commentary a quiet week calls for.

invented: [minor] It remains a remarkably unproductive conflict for everyone involved. (States the war's lack of results as fact; the briefing gives no outcome.)
comment: Clear and accurate on the lead item, with the guess about the Lancers properly hedged. But it runs short at about 50 words and the wit is thin and generic, especially in the second item, which also asserts an unsupported outcome.

invented: Tamsin knelt in the red-stained dirt of the Lancers' camp (Places Tamsin at the camp beside the body. The briefing says the Lancers still hold the camp, so this is an unsupported and implausible event.) | her father’s heavy, notched blade (Introduces a weapon the briefing never mentions.) | [minor] his mangled arm, the jagged scar from Rook Malley’s initial strike (The briefing says Joska was maimed but does not say which body part.) | [minor] the pirate captain’s banner fluttering nearby (Adds a banner as invented scene detail.) | [minor] The metal was still warm from the struggle (Embellishes the fight with an implied immediacy the briefing does not give.)
comment: The ending correctly turns Tamsin toward the new captain. But the scene invents her presence in the enemy-held camp and a signature blade, and leans on stock clichés like white knuckles and lifeless eyes.

invented: This follows their expansion into the region. (The briefing reports one trading post; it mentions no prior expansion into the region.) | [minor] The Tarn Union continues to grow. (Ongoing growth is inferred from a single trading post but stated as fact.)
comment: The prose is flat and generic, with almost none of the dry, wry Ilse Varrow persona. It also invents a prior 'expansion into the region' and states the Tarn Union's growth as fact rather than as a guess.

invented: [minor] No one claims it yet. (The briefing does not say whether anyone has claimed the abandoned camp; this aftermath is stated as fact.) | [minor] The Glimmer Coast Company continues to report profits. (Ongoing profits are not in the briefing; this extends a joke from an earlier bulletin into present fact.) | [minor] as planned (The briefing does not say the caravan's arrival was planned.)
comment: There is only one new item, yet the bulletin pads to three by restating old news (the ford arrival, the salt-flat war) as current reports, which the task forbids. The voice is flatter and less wry than the earlier bulletins, and it echoes their salt-price lines.

invented: The Grass fires in the south continue. (Briefing reports nothing new; claims an old event is ongoing now.) | The Kinn are moving, but not in a way that suggests conflict. (Presents the Kinn's movement as current news with an unsupported assessment.) | [minor] Their fires are slow, and their steps are slower. (Embellishes the pace of the fires and the Kinn's movement.) | [minor] but they are watching (States the Ashen Hand's intent as fact rather than as a guess.)
comment: The bulletin re-presents the old grass fires and Kinn migration as ongoing news, which contradicts the quiet briefing. The voice is flat and lacks the dry wit of earlier bulletins; the faction-count opener is the only solid part.

invented: He was last seen heading toward Lowmere. (The briefing never says where Quell was last seen. It only implies a possible link between him and Lowmere.) | No one claims responsibility. (This contradicts the briefing, which attributes the burning to the Black Fen Raiders.) | The fire was reported by a merchant ship passing through. (The merchant ship and how the fire was reported are invented.) | The Rim Dispatch has fewer reporters than the Brine Coast League. (The briefing gives settlement counts, not reporter counts. The comparison is invented.) | They rely on tips from traders. (This is an invented claim about how the Dispatch operates.) | [minor] The station (Calling the Dispatch a 'station' is an unsupported embellishment.) | [minor] before he vanished (This treats a disappearance as fact. The briefing only says the Dispatch is looking for news of him.)
comment: Five major inventions: a last-seen location, an unclaimed attack that contradicts the briefing, a merchant ship, reporter counts, and trader tips. The voice is also flat, not wry, and oddly distant, with the reporter calling her own paper 'they'.

invented: [minor] No goods move through their gates. (Extends 'closed to outsiders' to a total halt on goods.) | [minor] No traders are seen near their settlements. (An implied consequence stated as an observed fact.) | [minor] The cold snap continues to affect the northern basin. (The briefing does not say the cold snap is ongoing.) | [minor] but only among themselves now (An inference from the market closure, stated as fact.)
comment: Only one item is new, yet the bulletin pads with two old-news paragraphs presented as current, recycling the patrol-payment joke and dropping the sardonic voice almost entirely. The lead item is also inflated with unsupported consequences.

invented: The barge belonged to the Calder Combine (The briefing does not say who owned the grain barge.)
comment: The bulletin is clear and correctly treats the shuttles and harvest as background, but it invents Calder Combine ownership of the barge. The voice is generic, with little of Ilse's dry wit.

invented: They blame raiders, but no one has claimed responsibility. (Invents a new fact that no one claimed the raid, and casts doubt on the raiders, which the briefing states as fact.) | [minor] still rankles (Adds an ongoing grievance that the briefing does not report.) | [minor] The gorge remains a contested stretch of road. (Embellishes the gorge as contested ground.) | [minor] This follows their envoys’ recent visits to outlander towns. (Implies a sequence or link between the visits and the tolls that the briefing does not state.)
comment: The lead item is right, but the bulletin pads with a third paragraph that restates the Empire item. It also invents that no one claimed the wagon raid. The voice is flatter and less wry than in the earlier bulletins.

invented: The Lantern Accord claims it’s a gift from a distant patron. (Invented claim about the sculpture's origin; no such statement is in the briefing.) | The Lantern Accord’s trade fair is still set for next week, as promised. (Invents a schedule and contradicts the timeline: the fair was already 'next week' in an earlier bulletin.) | [minor] Traders are debating its worth, though few seem to agree on much else. (Embellishes 'talk of the traders' with a debate and disagreement.) | [minor] has drawn a crowd (Adds scale that the briefing does not give.) | [minor] which is not unusual for them (Inference about the gang's habits, stated as fact.)
comment: Two invented facts: the 'distant patron' claim and the fair 'still set for next week', which contradicts the earlier bulletin. The second paragraph also pads with old news in a flat voice that has almost none of Ilse's dry wit.

invented: His body was found with a knife in his back (The briefing gives no method of death and no discovery of a body.) | no one claims to have seen him alive since (This is an invented detail about witnesses.) | neither has yet managed to take a settlement (The briefing says nothing about the war's progress or any settlements taken.) | [minor] Both sides remain stubborn (This embellishes the war with an unsupported description of manner.) | [minor] The war, as before, shows no sign of ending soon (This is an inference about the war's outcome stated as fact.) | Malley’s Lancers have not made any new claims or threats. The pirates are quiet (The briefing does not report on the Lancers' recent behaviour.) | [minor] which is unusual for them (This is an inferred characterisation of the Lancers stated as fact.)
comment: The bulletin copies the duplicated briefing line almost verbatim, so it reads as redundant and robotic. It invents several major details: the knife in the back, the absence of witnesses, no settlements taken, and the pirates going quiet. It also lacks the sardonic voice the persona calls for.

invented: She would find Malley. (Contradicts the briefing: Malley died in the same fight. The heir's purpose rests on a dead man.) | She would carve her name into his flesh. (Revenge aimed at Malley, who is already dead per the briefing.) | the jagged scar across his cheek (A specific wound the briefing does not give; it says only that Joska was maimed.) | She had seen that scar before—on Malley’s face, mirrored like a cruel joke. (Invented physical detail about Malley, not in the briefing.) | his old combat knife, the one he’d used to carve his name into the wall (An invented item and an invented past event.) | [minor] She pressed it to her palm, then to her thigh. The blood bloomed fast. (Self-wounding ritual is added action not grounded in the briefing.)
comment: The scene ends with Tamsin vowing to hunt Malley, who the briefing says died alongside Joska. It ignores the real threat, the Lancers' new captain, and piles on invented scars, a knife and backstory. The self-cutting and 'cruel joke' imagery tip into melodrama.

invented: [minor] this is the Dispatch's first bulletin (The briefing says only that this is Ilse's first bulletin, not the Dispatch's first ever.)
comment: Accurate and drily witty, with guesses properly hedged. The third paragraph turns the faction counts into a sensible quiet-week item, but it slightly misstates the first bulletin as the Dispatch's rather than Ilse's.

The bulletin is accurate and well ordered. It leads with the abandoned camp, keeps the salt-flats war as background, and gets its quiet-week wit from the real settlement counts. The voice is dry and fitting but slightly less sharp than the earlier bulletins, and the closing 'arithmetic' line hints at a decline the briefing doesn't strictly show.

invented: [minor] The tally stands where it stood. (Implies the faction counts are unchanged, but no earlier figures were given.) | [minor] which may be why they keep to homesteads (Stretches one raid on two homesteads into a habit; the cause is hedged but the pattern is stated as fact.)
comment: A sound quiet-week bulletin that comments drily on the faction counts and the colony's silence, with clear structure and no padding. The 'tally stands' line and the 'keep to homesteads' generalisation stretch the briefing slightly, and the opening is a little flat.

All three items are reported plainly and accurately, and every guess is clearly framed as one. The dry, understated voice lets the missing reporter and the Lowmere pullback hint at each other without inventing a link; only the 'suspect… suspicion' echo is slightly clumsy.

invented: [minor] those markets were among the few places a hungry farmer could find grain, at a price (Embellishes the earlier furs-for-grain line: 'among the few places' is added, and the direction of that trade is ambiguous.) | [minor] now also has the fewest visitors (An inference from the closed markets, stated as fact.)
comment: A sardonic, well-paced lead with a good understated joke, and the old news is correctly framed as background. However, it stretches one new item to three paragraphs, which is mild padding, and it embellishes the grain-market role slightly.

This is accurate and stays within the briefing, and the robbery is tied wryly to the earlier harvest report with every guess framed as a guess. The second paragraph's 'busy counting' line is a little muddled, and 'all sitting quietly behind their walls' could be misread as covering every faction rather than just the Throne.

invented: [minor] Vex's Crew, with two settlements, has said nothing at all (The briefing records no statement or silence from Vex's Crew; it is an inference stated as fact.)
comment: Dry, clear and accurate on the toll news and the faction arithmetic. It breaks the brief by recycling earlier lines: 'polite smiles and long scrolls' and the escort-eyesight joke are reused outright rather than freshly written.

It leads correctly with the single new item and fills the quiet week with dry commentary on the faction counts, with every guess framed as a guess. It invents no facts, keeps the persona's wry voice, and only nods to old news as background.

invented: It is day 288 of Decembary (Day 288 is the day of the year; the phrasing misstates the date as the 288th day of Decembary.)
comment: Dry, well-ordered bulletin that leads correctly with Malley's death, frames its guesses properly and handles the war as background. The garbled date phrasing ('day 288 of Decembary') misstates the briefing and caps the score.

invented: [minor] They carried Joska home to Cinder Rest on a stretcher. (Recovery of the body is plausible staging, but the briefing never says it was brought home.) | [minor] unwound the old pit wraps from his knuckles (Embellishes his pit-fighter backstory with a specific item the briefing never mentions.) | [minor] Lene's hands shook too badly to hold the shovel (Invented action for Lene at a burial the briefing does not describe.)
comment: The restrained, physical detail fits RimWorld, and the ending gives a clear resolve. However, the sequence breaks: Tamsin unwinds the wraps from Joska's knuckles after the grave is already packed, which undercuts the scene's central image.
